# Mosaic ERP

Mosaic ERP is an MIT-licensed, interview-native operational ERP for evidence-backed core retailer work. It turns plain-language owner answers into real controls and supports buying, receiving, selling, returns/refunds, stock, cash, supplier bills/payments, reconciliation, period close and core accounting reports. Built-in deterministic chat is the default, and users can optionally connect their own AI provider. Setup and configuration are guided in chat; provider secrets use a masked secure step and never enter chat, logs, exports, or audit detail. New in Preview in v1.3.0: the fine-tuned local assistant runs on the shop's own machine; it can understand, draft and explain ERP actions, and every action requires the owner's explicit confirmation of the exact rendered payload. Measured on the frozen development contract: all constrained outputs were schema-valid, every tested unsafe request failed closed, and label accuracy was 84 to 86 percent, so drafts must be read before approval.

Current verified facts for the shipped v1.3.2 tree: guided setup; built-in deterministic chat by default; optional chat-guided bring-your-own AI-provider setup with masked secret handling; core retailer transactions; core accounting; fine-grained operational access; PostgreSQL restricted-runtime-role tenant isolation; concurrency and failure acceptance; strict Helm/deployment checks that fail closed on plain-HTTP hosted exposure; configuration-aware real Google/Microsoft OIDC routes with provider-published assets; one-download desktop apps for Windows and Apple Silicon Mac with the local assistant Preview bundled (sha256-pinned model artifacts, loopback-only serving, single-use owner-confirmed drafts, native benchmark evidence); a hardened hosted HTTPS path with the app port private behind a pinned Caddy edge. Each release's archives, checksums, container digests, signatures, SBOM/provenance and vulnerability-scan results live with that release and are never inferred from an earlier one.

Boundaries: statutory invoices, tax filing, e-invoicing and jurisdiction certification are excluded unless a separate local adapter/version is reviewed by the business owner or a named professional. Advanced retail, manufacturing, payroll and broad enterprise-suite modules are excluded. Operators own DNS/TLS, provider registration and secrets, managed PostgreSQL HA/PITR, restore drills, cluster failover/capacity evidence, monitoring and independent penetration testing before real hosted financial-data use. SQLite is for local evaluation or simple single-process use; concurrent production replicas require external PostgreSQL.
